- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent price spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% for high recent prices.
- After a spike (e.g., >88), model tends to overshoot downward in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for the first 7 days post-spike.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion zones (e.g., below 82–84) and fails to anticipate sharp drops; increase forecast sensitivity to recent low prices.
- Sentiment history is always neutral (0.00), so no sentiment-based adjustment is triggered — but if sentiment were positive, model should be slightly more bullish; if negative, slightly more bearish.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in capturing true price drops — especially in the 10–15 day window — so adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.0% for days 10–15 if true price is falling.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high prices — if last 3–5 days are high, reduce forecast peak by 1–2% to prevent over-optimism.
- If true price drops below 80 after a spike, model often fails to recognize the new support — apply a 1–2% downward correction for days 10–15 post-drop.
